transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’ve felt this heavy, low mood every day for over a year, like I just can’t shake feeling down no matter what I do. It just feels like a constant weight is always sitting on me, and I can't seem to get past it.

During this past year, have there been stretches of 2 months or longer when your mood felt mostly normal, or has the low mood been there nearly every day the whole time? Have there also been any separate periods lasting at least 2 weeks when it got much worse than your usual baseline?

No, there haven't been any breaks—it has been there nearly every single day for the past year without any periods of feeling normal. It's just been a steady, continuous struggle ever since my wife left, rather than coming in separate, worse waves.
Has this ongoing low mood significantly affected your work, daily responsibilities, or relationships? If so, what has changed the most?

It’s completely derailed my life—I went from being a top sales performer to missing deadlines and targets, and my boss recently warned me my job is on the line. Outside of work, I've stopped seeing my friends entirely and I'm neglecting basic things like laundry and paying my bills on time.

Did these symptoms start within about 3 months after your wife left, and have they stayed closely tied to that stressor rather than feeling like a long-standing depression that would continue even if the situation improved?

Yes, everything started pretty much right after my wife left with our son about a year ago. But now, it feels like a deep, heavy depression that is constantly with me, and I don't think it would just lift even if my situation suddenly improved.

When your depression is at its worst, have you ever heard or seen things others don’t, or become completely convinced of things like being worthless or guilty in a way others say isn’t true? Have you also been unable to do basic self-care, like eating, bathing, or getting out of bed, because of how severe it gets?

No, I don't hear or see things that aren't there, but I am constantly consumed by guilt, feeling like a terrible husband and father who ruined my family. I also really struggle with basic self-care, often skipping meals because I have no appetite and finding that even getting out of bed or showering feels like I'm moving in slow motion through mud.

Over the past 2 weeks, have you had very little interest or pleasure in things and several other symptoms like poor sleep, low energy, trouble concentrating, or feeling slowed down nearly every day? If yes, how many of these symptoms have been present?

Yes, I've been struggling with all of those symptoms nearly every day, and it has actually been going on for over a year, not just the last two weeks. I have absolutely no interest in things I used to love like basketball, I wake up in the middle of the night unable to sleep, and my brain is in such a fog at work that I feel like I'm constantly moving in slow motion through mud.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting or killing yourself? If yes, have you made any plans or taken any steps toward it?

Yes, especially late at night, I catch myself thinking that it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. I've even gone as far as sitting there counting out my leftover pain pills, wondering if taking them all at once would finally let everyone move on.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a sustained severe depressive syndrome with depressed mood, marked anhedonia, insomnia, low appetite, psychomotor slowing, impaired concentration, excessive guilt, severe functional decline, and suicidal ideation with consideration of overdose. Psychotic symptoms were denied. Although symptoms began after his wife left, he reports the condition has evolved into a pervasive major depressive state that would not simply remit if the stressor improved, making a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms the best fit among the provided candidates.
